title: Reading Contractions
keyIdea: A contraction is two words squashed into one short word. Some letters drop out, and an apostrophe ( ' ) goes in their place. I am becomes I'm, do not becomes don't, and we will becomes we'll. To read a contraction, say the two long words in your head: can't means cannot, it's means it is.

kid: Sometimes we squash two words into one. I am turns into I'm. It is quicker to say.
When the words squash, some letters drop out. A little mark goes in the gap. It is called an apostrophe.
The apostrophe sits right where the letters went. In don't, it sits where the o of not was.
When you read a short word like can't, think of the long words. Can't means cannot. It's means it is.
adult: In England, Year 1 word reading asks children to read words with contractions, such as I'm, I'll and we'll. They should know that the apostrophe stands for the letter or letters left out. In Year 2 they learn to spell these words with the apostrophe in the right place, so reading them well now helps with writing next year.

The words to use: a contraction is a short form of two words. The apostrophe of omission marks where letters have been left out. Not is the most common partner (don't, can't, didn't, isn't), along with am, is, are, will and have (I'm, she's, they're, we'll, I've). Can't comes from cannot, which is already one word, so only the n and o drop.

Common mistakes: putting the apostrophe between the two words (do'nt, not don't); leaving it out (Im, dont); keeping the dropped letter too (I'am); and mixing up we'll with well, or it's with its. Be careful not to teach it's and its with rules about owning yet. At this age the simple test is: can you say it is in its place?

In the lab your child taps out the letters that drop and drags the apostrophe into the gap. Then they unzip short words to their long forms, pick the right gap in dont, shes and theyre, spot three contractions in a tiny story, and squash two words in a sentence into one. Every drag also has a big button.

familyTip: When you read together, stop at a word like don't or I'm. Ask: which two words are hiding in here? Cover the apostrophe with a finger and ask which letters went missing.

visual.caption: Contraction or not? Drag each card to a box, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: squash two words into one, unzip short words, find the apostrophe's gap, spot contractions in a story.

practice.hint: Say the two long words. Which letter dropped out of I am?
practice.explain: I'm is I am squashed together. The apostrophe sits where the a of am was.

practice.prompt: Tom reads {a} words with an apostrophe for missing letters, like don't. He also reads {b} words with no apostrophe. How many contractions does he read?
practice.hint: A contraction has an apostrophe for missing letters. Count only those words.
practice.explain: Only the {a} words with an apostrophe are contractions. The {b} other words are not.

practice.prompt: Which one has the apostrophe in the right place?
practice.hint: Do not loses the o from not. Where was that o?
practice.explain: Don't puts the apostrophe where the o of not was, between the n and the t.

practice.prompt: Kim writes {n} sentences. In each one she squashes do not into don't. How many apostrophes does she write?
practice.hint: Each don't has one apostrophe. How many don'ts are there?
practice.explain: Each don't needs one apostrophe, so {n} sentences need {n} apostrophes.

pool.hint: Which word has the letters c, a, n, n, o, t?
pool.explain: Can't is short for cannot. The n and o drop out and the apostrophe goes in their place.

pool.prompt: What does it's mean in: It's raining?
pool.hint: Try saying it is in its place. Does the sentence still make sense?
pool.explain: It's is it is: the i of is drops out. It is raining makes sense.

pool.prompt: What does the apostrophe in we'll show?
pool.hint: We'll is short for two words. What happened to some letters?
pool.explain: We'll is we will. The w and i drop out and the apostrophe shows where.

pool.prompt: What is the short way to say they are?
pool.hint: The a of are drops out. Put the apostrophe where it was.
pool.explain: They are becomes they're. The apostrophe takes the place of the a.

pool.prompt: Which word is a contraction? We're going home.
pool.hint: Look for the word with the little mark in it.
pool.explain: We're has an apostrophe. It is short for we are.

pool.prompt: A story has {a} contractions on page 1 and {b} on page 2. How many contractions are in the story?
pool.hint: Add the contractions on both pages.
pool.explain: {a} and {b} make {=a+b} contractions. Each one hides two words.

pool.prompt: Sam writes I'm {n} times. Each time the a of am drops out. How many letters did he leave out in all?
pool.hint: One letter goes each time. How many times did he write I'm?
pool.explain: One a drops out each time, so {n} times leaves out {n} letters.

pool.prompt: Which is right: I'm or I'am?
pool.hint: The apostrophe takes the place of a letter. Should the letter stay too?
pool.explain: I'm is right. The apostrophe replaces the a, so the a does not stay.
